answers: The B10 product share, reference residual and complete service-basket difference are distinct quantities. B13’s allocated route net benefits can reverse order without changing either full physical route. Figure3 includes a different quality basis; the separate fixed-reference derivation isolates the weights.

Changed services require actual top-up or a new comparison; changed performance, references or uncancelled disposal changes the net terms. The B10 partial-use case and separate paper heat/electricity compensation show why merely rescaling an old credit is insufficient.

A common positive multiplier k preserves the sign of M−H; k=0 collapses strict order. Different weights permit but do not guarantee reversal. Positivity here allows the quantities to be called net benefits, not a universal restriction on sign-preserving multiplication.

Capacity evidence changes quantities and destinations of local and imported waste and actual heat/electricity supply. Equal total feed energy needs further delivery conditions. B cannot supply that evidence or replace the activity change, just as B11 purchasing reassignment does not prove extra hydro generation.
